A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same perception-coherence research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison: Appendices A–E in v2 and A–F in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original toy-data simulations, image-retrieval and CIFAR100 classification results, and batch-size, model-size, and temperature ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds a two-moon classification study, revised CIFAR100 results, and model-computation measurements.

M1.justification: The sigmoid soft-ranking procedure, normalized ranking loss in Equations (3)–(4), and classification loss combination remain unchanged. The added experiments and augmentation do not introduce a new proposed method component.

E1.justification: New Section 5.2 extends two-moon data from geometric configuration transfer to neural binary classification. CIFAR10, the CUB200 subset, and CIFAR100 coverage remain. SVHN appears only as an unexplained heading in the new computation table; no SVHN learning experiment is documented.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds ReviewKD, DIST, TTM, and VRM to the CIFAR100 comparison, substantially expanding comparison against recent methods across all three teacher–student pairs. The earlier comparator rows and retrieval comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: CIFAR100 training adds RandAug to match VRM's setting while retaining the stated model pairs, 240 epochs, and batch size 64. The new two-moon study introduces a 400/400 training/test split and frozen-feature classification evaluations at ten checkpoints. Appendix F adds MAC measurement using ptflops.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds a controlled checkpoint analysis relating perception coherence to downstream classification accuracy. Appendix F examines teacher–student computation costs. These supplement the unchanged batch-size, student-size, and temperature ablations.

E5.justification: The new checkpoint analysis reports Pearson correlation and a fitted linear trend in Figure 6. Both versions retain five independent CIFAR100 runs and the existing uncertainty-reporting practices; the ten checkpoints are not additional independent runs.

E6.justification: The proposed method's CIFAR100 accuracies change from 68.64/75.62/76.04 in v2 Table 3 to 71.10/78.59/79.14 with RandAug in v3 Table 4; these are replacement results under changed conditions. Among v3 distillation methods, VRM leads two columns and the proposed method leads ShuffleNetV1. New results include checkpoint accuracy/coherence pairs, reported correlation 0.920, and MAC counts. Retrieval and existing ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.5 now explicitly requires P(X in A) > 0, whereas v2 required only a nonempty A. This supplies a condition needed for the bound involving inverse probability mass. The other formal results and Appendix A–D proofs remain unchanged, including Appendix D's older theorem restatement.

C1.justification: The abstract now qualifies the comparative-performance claim with 'particularly class-unaware ones.' The central contributions—probabilistic perception coherence, ranking-based transfer, and theoretical guarantees—remain the same.

C2.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands applicability and practical discussion: it explicitly targets heterogeneous distillation, excludes broader self-supervised comparisons, and discusses cubic training cost and proposed GPU parallelization. Section 5.2 adds an interpretation of coherence as a downstream-performance proxy. Existing capacity limitations and topology-related discussion are retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents the new probe's network architecture, optimizer, learning rate, training stages, and checkpoint schedule; identifies the RandAug implementation source and ptflops profiler; and replaces the anonymous code pointer with a named GitHub repository link. Existing hardware and most implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: A new class-awareness paragraph contrasts the method with reused-teacher-classifier and CrossKD approaches. References also add ReviewKD, TTM, VRM, and ptflops. This is a focused extension of the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 inserts the controlled-study and practical-scope sections, adds Appendix E.2 and Appendix F, and updates numbering, citations, and publication/author information. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the coherence/accuracy plot and table (Figure 6 and Table 1), adds the computation table (Table 8), and expands the CIFAR100 comparison table. Existing graphics are retained with repositioning and renumbering; publication headers and table placement also change.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful controlled evidence connecting coherence with downstream accuracy, includes recent comparators with a matched RandAug setting for VRM, and clarifies scope and reproducibility. These improve a largely retained paper incrementally. Comparisons with older baseline rows remain limited by differing augmentation, and the unexplained SVHN heading reduces the clarity of the new computation table.
